question: If we multiply (-6ab) and (11ab²c), then we get:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Multiply constants: −6 × 11 = −66

Add powers of a: 1 + 1 = 2 → a²

Add powers of b: 1 + 2 = 3 → b³

Power of c remains 1 → c

Combine: −66a²b³c

**∴ Answer = −66a²b³c**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First term = (−6ab)

Second term = (11ab²c)

**Formula used:**

Product of monomials = (Product of numerical coefficients) × (Product of algebraic variables)

Law of indices: xm × xⁿ = xm⁺ⁿ

 −6ab × 11ab2c = −66a2b3c 
 
 Group numerical & literal factors Final Result: −66a²b³c 

**Calculations:**

Product = (−6ab) × (11ab²c)

⇒ Product = (−6 × 11) × (a × a) × (b × b²) × c ⇒ Product = (−66) × (a¹⁺¹) × (b¹⁺²) × c ⇒ Product = −66 × a² × b³ × c ⇒ Product = −66a²b³c

**∴ The correct answer is (2).**
